purpose: New neutral diffuse material atlas for an existing closed 3D lotus leaf; not a scene/frame replacement
prompt: Generate one square botanical PBR diffuse/albedo atlas for a REAL modeled lotus leaf, not a film frame or a scene. Full square filled with continuous mature Nelumbo nucifera leaf tissue: no silhouette, no background, no transparency, no border, no writing. The renderer will use an inscribed circular UV area with its stem insertion exactly at (50%,50%) and radius49% of the square. Make 19 principal slender radial veins starting at that precise centre, dividing into a very fine irregular branching vein network through the matte waxy tissue. Natural restrained sage/olive green, subtle chlorophyll variation, a few barely visible pale age flecks, fine realistic leaf cells, thin slightly paler vein ribs; not luminous lime, neon, painted rings or perfectly periodic stripes. Neutral flat cross-polarized scan lighting only, no directional light, no folds shaded into the image, no cast shadows, no specular glints, no sunspots or water droplets. Physical tissue represents a 45cm wide leaf; tiny secondary veins must be much finer than principal veins. The real 3D mesh already supplies all folds, curled rims, thickness and raised primary ribs, so this atlas must be mostly flat neutral DIFFUSE REFLECTANCE. Tissue continues to all four square corners without a leaf outline. Photographic macro material detail, high resolution2048x2048 square.
